category: User Interface, Customization, Collaboration & Recent Features
description: Commands that shape the working environment and connect AutoCAD to the cloud: loading and transferring CUIx customization, ribbon and tool palettes, workspaces, the command line and clean screen, AutoComplete, the system variable monitor and SYSVDLG, file tabs and the Start tab, colour theme, UI locking, Quick Properties, DesignCenter navigation, plus the features added between 2019 and 2026 - Count, Trace, Markup Import and Markup Assist, Share and Shared Views, Push to Autodesk Docs, save/open from web and mobile, Activity Insights, the Autodesk Assistant, Command Macros, the Performance Analyzer, new-feature highlighting, the App Store, Action Recorder input requests, floating drawing windows and WEBLOAD.

tools.name: CUILOAD
tools.description: Opens the Load/Unload Customizations dialog to load a partial customization file (.cuix) into the session - adding its ribbon tabs, toolbars, menus, macros and workspaces alongside the main acad.cuix - or to unload one; CUIUNLOAD opens the same dialog on the unload side, and MENULOAD/MENUUNLOAD are the legacy aliases. Company customization is normally deployed this way (or as the Enterprise CUIx set in Options > Files) rather than by editing acad.cuix, so upgrades do not overwrite it.
tools.usage:
CUILOAD / CUIUNLOAD
(Load/Unload Customizations dialog: Loaded Customization Groups list; File Name with Browse; Load / Unload)
Customization file roles: Main (acad.cuix), Enterprise (read-only shared, ENTERPRISEMENU), Partial (loaded under the main), Express Tools (acetmain.cuix)
AutoLISP: (command "_.CUILOAD" "C:/std/office.cuix")  or  (menucmd ...) for menu state

parameters.name: customization group
parameters.description: The name inside the CUIx (not the file name); two files with the same group name cannot both be loaded.

parameters.name: MENUNAME / ENTERPRISEMENU
parameters.description: Read-only variables giving the main and enterprise CUIx paths; set the enterprise file in OPTIONS > Files > Customization Files.

parameters.name: .mnl
parameters.description: A LISP file with the same base name as the CUIx loads automatically with it - the place for the LISP that its macros call.

tools.example:
CUILOAD
(Browse: C:\std\office.cuix, Load, Close)
; the ribbon tab defined in office.cuix now appears in the current workspace once added via CUI > Workspaces
tools.notes: Partial CUIx files loaded interactively are remembered in the profile (registry) and reload on every start; the /p startup switch with a profile .arg deploys the same state to other users. Ribbon tabs from a partial file must be added to a workspace (CUI editor) before they show.

tools.name: CUIEXPORT
tools.description: Opens the Customize User Interface editor on its Transfer tab with the main CUIx on the left and a new empty file on the right, so ribbon panels, toolbars, menus, commands, macros, shortcut keys or workspaces can be dragged into it and saved as a separate .cuix; CUIIMPORT opens the same tab with an existing file on the right for dragging elements into the main file. This is how customizations are moved between machines, releases and users without copying the whole acad.cuix.
tools.usage:
CUIEXPORT   (CUI editor > Transfer tab, main CUIx left, new file right; drag items; Save As .cuix)
CUIIMPORT   (CUI editor > Transfer tab, main CUIx left, Open... a .cuix on the right; drag items to the left; Apply)

parameters.name: Transfer tab tree
parameters.description: Workspaces, Quick Access Toolbars, Ribbon (Tabs/Panels), Toolbars, Menus, Quick Properties, Rollover Tooltips, Shortcut Menus, Keyboard Shortcuts, Double Click Actions, Mouse Buttons, LISP Files, Legacy, Partial Customization Files, Command List.

parameters.name: migration
parameters.description: The Migrate Custom Settings tool at first run of a new release transfers CUIx changes automatically; CUIEXPORT/IMPORT is the manual alternative.

tools.example:
CUIEXPORT
(drag the 'Office Tools' ribbon panel and the three custom commands to the right pane; Save As C:\std\office_panel.cuix)
tools.notes: Commands referenced by macros must be transferred too (they live in the Command List) or the buttons show a missing-command icon. Workspaces transferred without their tabs/panels are empty.

tools.name: QUICKCUI
tools.description: Opens the Customize User Interface editor in its collapsed 'quick' state showing only the command list and the properties pane, for fast edits to a command's macro, name, image or description without the full customization tree. The full editor is a click away (the expand arrow) and is what CUI opens.
tools.usage: QUICKCUI  (collapsed CUI editor: Command List with search, Properties pane, Button Image pane)

parameters.name: Command List
parameters.description: Filter by category or search; Create a New Command; edit Name, Description, Macro, Element ID, images.

parameters.name: Macro syntax
parameters.description: ^C^C cancel, _ English name, . native command, ; Enter, \ pause, ^P menu echo toggle, $M= DIESEL, (lisp) inline.

tools.example:
QUICKCUI
(search 'ZoomExtents'; edit macro to ^C^C_zoom;_e;_regen; Apply)
tools.notes: Changes are written to the CUIx immediately on Apply and a backup (.bak) of the CUIx is kept. Macro edits affect every ribbon button and toolbar that references the command.

tools.name: RIBBON
tools.description: Displays the ribbon after it was closed (RIBBONCLOSE hides it), restoring the tab set of the current workspace. Ribbon behaviour is tuned by system variables: RIBBONSTATE reports it, RIBBONDOCKEDHEIGHT sets the height when panels are shown, RIBBONCONTEXTSELECT / RIBBONCONTEXTSELLIM control contextual tabs on selection, RIBBONSELECTMODE keeps the selection after a contextual-tab command, RIBBONICONRESIZE resizes icons and RIBBONBGLOAD loads tabs in the background. The minimise button cycles tabs-only, panel titles, panel buttons and full ribbon.
tools.usage:
RIBBON / RIBBONCLOSE
RIBBONSTATE = 0 closed | 1 displayed (read-only)
RIBBONCONTEXTSELECT = 0 no contextual tab on selection | 1 on single click | 2 on double click
RIBBONCONTEXTSELLIM = max objects (default 2500) for which contextual tabs are shown
RIBBONSELECTMODE = 0 selection cleared after a contextual tab command | 1 kept
RIBBONDOCKEDHEIGHT = 0 auto | 1-500 pixels
RIBBONICONRESIZE = 0 icons not resized | 1 resized for standard sizes (2023+)

parameters.name: customize
parameters.description: Right-click a tab or panel: Show Tabs / Show Panels, Undock, Float, or open CUI to add panels from partial CUIx files.

parameters.name: MENUBAR
parameters.description: 1 shows the classic pull-down menu bar above the ribbon.

tools.example:
RIBBONCLOSE
(work with the menu bar and toolbars)
RIBBON
RIBBONCONTEXTSELLIM 500
tools.notes: A missing ribbon after installing add-ins is usually a workspace without the tabs - switch workspace with WORKSPACE or WSCURRENT. Ribbon rendering is per profile; the /w switch starts with a named workspace.

tools.name: TOOLPALETTES
tools.description: Opens the Tool Palettes window (Ctrl+3): tabbed palettes holding tools that insert blocks, apply hatches, run commands (with macros) or set properties, organised in palette groups. Tools are created by dragging objects out of the drawing or from DesignCenter, and every tool has editable properties (right-click > Properties: source file, block name, scale, rotation, prompt for rotation, explode, layer/colour/linetype overrides, auxiliary scale by DIMSCALE or PLOTSCALE). TOOLPALETTESCLOSE closes it; TPSTATE reports the state; palettes are stored as .atc files in the tool palette path (Options > Files) and can be shared read-only across a network.
tools.usage:
TOOLPALETTES  (Ctrl+3; alias TP)
TOOLPALETTESCLOSE
(right-click the title bar: Allow Docking, Auto-hide, Transparency, View Options, New Palette, Rename, Customize Palettes, Customize Commands, palette group names)
(right-click a tool: Cut/Copy/Delete/Rename, Update tool image, Specify image, Properties)

parameters.name: Block tools
parameters.description: Source file + block name; inserting with the tool uses the tool's scale/rotation/layer settings and can prompt for rotation.

parameters.name: Command tools
parameters.description: A macro string as in CUI (^C^C_layiso;) with an image; created by dragging a toolbar button or via Customize Commands.

parameters.name: Hatch / gradient / material / visual style tools
parameters.description: Drag a hatch, material or visual style onto a palette; dropping it on an object applies it.

parameters.name: Tool palette path
parameters.description: OPTIONS > Files > Tool Palettes File Locations; several folders can be listed, read-only network folders make palettes shared.

tools.example:
TOOLPALETTES
(right-click title > New Palette 'DOORS'; drag the DOOR_900 block reference from the drawing onto it; right-click the tool > Properties: Prompt for rotation Yes, Layer A-DOOR)
(drag from the palette into a plan to insert)
tools.notes: Tools keep the source file path, so blocks that come from a moved library show a broken tool until the path is updated (Properties or REDIR-like batch editing of the .atc XML). Palettes export/import as .xtp files through CUSTOMIZE.

tools.name: TPNAVIGATE
tools.description: Displays a specific tool palette or palette group by name from the command line, opening the Tool Palettes window if needed - what CUI macros and LISP use to bring up the right palette for a task (e.g. the Electrical symbols palette when the user starts an electrical command).
tools.usage:
TPNAVIGATE
Specify tool palette to display or [palette Group]: <palette name> | G then Enter palette group to display: <group name>

parameters.name: palette name
parameters.description: Case-insensitive; must exist in the current or any group.

parameters.name: Group
parameters.description: Switches the visible group (a set of palettes).

tools.example:
; CUI macro
^C^C_TPNAVIGATE;DOORS
; AutoLISP
(command "_.TPNAVIGATE" "_G" "Architectural")
tools.notes: Palette groups are defined in CUSTOMIZE > Palette Groups. Names with spaces are accepted as typed.

tools.name: CUSTOMIZE
tools.description: Opens the Customize dialog for tool palettes: the Palettes tab creates, renames, deletes and reorders palettes and imports/exports them as .xtp files (a palette plus its images), and the Palette Groups tab builds groups (trees of palettes), sets the current group and imports/exports groups as .xpg files. It is the sharing and deployment interface for palettes, as CUI is for the ribbon.
tools.usage:
CUSTOMIZE  (Tool Palettes title bar > Customize Palettes)
(Customize dialog: Palettes tab [list; right-click: New Palette, Rename, Delete, Export..., Import...]; Palette Groups tab [tree; right-click: New Group, Rename, Delete, Set Current, Export..., Export All..., Import...])

parameters.name: .xtp
parameters.description: XML export of one palette with its tool definitions and images.

parameters.name: .xpg
parameters.description: Export of a palette group structure (references palettes by name).

parameters.name: Set Current
parameters.description: Makes a group the one displayed in the Tool Palettes window.

tools.example:
CUSTOMIZE
(Palettes tab: right-click DOORS > Export... C:\std\palettes\DOORS.xtp)
(on another machine: Import... DOORS.xtp)
tools.notes: Exported .xtp files embed absolute source paths of block tools; keep libraries on the same path or edit the XML. Read-only palette folders show a lock icon and cannot be modified by users - the recommended way to deploy standards.

tools.name: WORKSPACE
tools.description: Manages workspaces - named arrangements of ribbon tabs, toolbars, menus, palettes and their positions - from the command line: set one current, save the current arrangement under a name, open the CUI editor to edit, rename, delete, list, or open the settings. The shipped workspaces are Drafting & Annotation, 3D Basics and 3D Modeling; WSCURRENT holds the current name and can be set directly, which is what scripts and the /w startup switch do.
tools.usage:
WORKSPACE
Enter workspace option [setCurrent/SAveas/Edit/Rename/Delete/SEttings/?] <setCurrent>:
setCurrent: Enter name of workspace [?] <current>: <name>
WSCURRENT = "<workspace name>"   (system variable; setting it switches)
WSAUTOSAVE = 0 | 1 (save workspace changes automatically when switching)

parameters.name: SAveas
parameters.description: Save the current UI state as a new or existing workspace (same as WSSAVE).

parameters.name: Edit
parameters.description: Open CUI with the workspace selected for editing its contents.

parameters.name: SEttings
parameters.description: Open the Workspace Settings dialog (WSSETTINGS).

tools.example:
WSCURRENT
3D Modeling

; startup with a workspace
acad.exe /w "Drafting & Annotation"

; AutoLISP
(setvar "WSCURRENT" "Office 2D")
tools.notes: Workspaces live in the CUIx (main or enterprise/partial); the toolbar/palette positions are saved per workspace when 'Automatically save workspace changes' is on in WSSETTINGS, which is why users lose custom layouts when switching - save them first with WSSAVE.

tools.name: WSSAVE
tools.description: Saves the current interface arrangement - which ribbon tabs and panels are shown and in what order, which toolbars and palettes are open and where they are docked, menu bar state - as a named workspace in the main CUIx, creating a new one or overwriting an existing one after confirmation. It is the step to take after arranging the screen the way a task needs, before WORKSPACE switches away.
tools.usage:
WSSAVE
(Save Workspace dialog: Name field / drop-down of existing names; Save)
-WSSAVE  Enter name of workspace to save <current>: <name>

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: New name creates a workspace; an existing name asks to replace it.

tools.example:
(arrange the ribbon, open Properties and Layers palettes docked left)
WSSAVE
Office 2D
tools.notes: Saved into the main CUIx (acad.cuix in the user's roaming profile). To share, transfer the workspace with CUIEXPORT together with the tabs it references.

tools.name: WSSETTINGS
tools.description: Opens the Workspace Settings dialog: choose My Workspace (the one the status-bar button returns to), the order and separators of workspaces in the switching menu, whether each is displayed, and - the important one - what happens when switching: Do not save changes to workspace, or Automatically save workspace changes (WSAUTOSAVE).
tools.usage:
WSSETTINGS
(Workspace Settings dialog: My Workspace drop-down; Menu Display and Order list with Move Up/Down/Add Separator; Display checkboxes; When Switching Workspaces: Do not save changes / Automatically save workspace changes)

parameters.name: Automatically save workspace changes
parameters.description: Persists palette/toolbar positions into the workspace on every switch - convenient but overwrites deliberately saved layouts.

parameters.name: My Workspace
parameters.description: Target of the Workspace Switching menu's 'My Workspace' entry and of the status-bar quick button.

tools.example:
WSSETTINGS
(My Workspace: Office 2D; When switching: Do not save changes; OK)
tools.notes: Settings are stored in the CUIx, not the profile. Enterprise CUIx workspaces are read-only and cannot be auto-saved, which is a good way to keep a standard layout stable.

tools.name: COMMANDLINE
tools.description: Displays the command window (Ctrl+9) after COMMANDLINEHIDE closed it; the window floats above the drawing by default with a wrench menu for AutoComplete, AutoCorrect, transparency, prompt history lines (CLIPROMPTLINES), colours and input search options. Hiding it is common on small screens with dynamic input (DYNMODE) supplying prompts at the cursor, but scripts and LISP still run without it.
tools.usage:
COMMANDLINE  (Ctrl+9)
COMMANDLINEHIDE
(wrench icon: Input Search Options..., Lines of Prompt History, Input Settings [AutoComplete, AutoCorrect, Search System Variables, Search Content, Mid-string Search, Delay Time], Transparency..., Options...)
CLIPROMPTLINES = 0-50 temporary prompt lines above the floating command line
CLIPROMPTUPDATE = 0 | 1 (show messages while scripts/LISP run)

parameters.name: docking
parameters.description: Drag to the top or bottom edge to dock; docked mode shows the classic multi-line history.

parameters.name: F2
parameters.description: Expands the prompt history (or opens the Text Window when docked).

parameters.name: CMDINPUTHISTORYMAX
parameters.description: Number of previous inputs kept for the up-arrow recall (default 20).

tools.example:
COMMANDLINEHIDE
(use dynamic input prompts)
COMMANDLINE
tools.notes: In the Core Console there is no window - everything is the console. A hidden command line plus DYNMODE 0 leaves no visible prompts, a common support call.

tools.name: CLEANSCREENON
tools.description: Maximises the drawing area by hiding the ribbon, toolbars, palettes, status bar (optionally) and the title bar (Ctrl+0), leaving the command line and file tabs; CLEANSCREENOFF restores everything. CLEANSCREENSTATE reports the state. Useful for presentations, small laptop screens and screen recordings; the status-bar visibility in clean screen is set in OPTIONS > Display.
tools.usage:
CLEANSCREENON  (Ctrl+0)
CLEANSCREENOFF (Ctrl+0)
CLEANSCREENSTATE = 0 | 1 (read-only)
tools.example:
CLEANSCREENON
(present the model with ShowMotion)
CLEANSCREENOFF
tools.notes: Palettes set to auto-hide stay reachable. The ribbon's own minimise button is the milder alternative when only the toolbars are in the way.

tools.name: INPUTSEARCHOPTIONS
tools.description: Opens the Input Search Options dialog that controls the command-line suggestion list: AutoComplete of command and system-variable names, AutoCorrect of misspelled commands, whether system variables and drawing content (blocks, layers, hatch patterns, text/dimension/visual styles) are searched, mid-string search, the delay before the list appears (INPUTSEARCHDELAY) and sorting by usage. Typing 'DOOR' then picking a block from the list inserts it, which makes the command line a content search box.
tools.usage:
INPUTSEARCHOPTIONS  (command line wrench > Input Search Options)
(dialog: Enable AutoComplete; Enable AutoCorrect [remember corrections after n misspellings]; Search System Variables; Search Content at Command Line [content types checkboxes]; Enable Mid-string Search; Sort suggestions by usage / alphabetically; Delay time ms)
INPUTSEARCHDELAY = 100-10000 ms (default 300)
INPUTSEARCHOPTIONFLAGS = bit sum storing the checkbox states

parameters.name: Mid-string search
parameters.description: Typing LAY finds LAYER and also XCLIPFRAME-like names containing the string.

parameters.name: Search Content
parameters.description: Blocks, layers, hatch patterns, text styles, dimension styles, visual styles listed with icons; selecting one runs the matching command (INSERT, LAYER set current, HATCH...).

parameters.name: AutoCorrect list
parameters.description: Corrections learned are stored in AutoCorrectUserDB.pgp next to acad.pgp.

tools.example:
INPUTSEARCHOPTIONS
(disable Search Content for large drawings where the list lags; Delay 500; OK)
tools.notes: Suggestions are also driven by acad.pgp aliases. In AutoCAD LT the same dialog exists. Disable AutoComplete when running scripts through the command line interactively, since partial input can match unexpectedly - scripts themselves are unaffected.

tools.name: SYSVARMONITOR
tools.description: Opens the System Variable Monitor (2016+): a list of watched system variables with their preferred values and current values, highlighting any that differ, with Reset All to restore them, Edit List to choose which variables are monitored, and notification options (balloon and status-bar icon when a monitored variable changes, e.g. by a LISP routine or a drawing's settings). SYSMON turns monitoring on or off. Typical watch list: FILEDIA, CMDDIA, PICKADD, PICKFIRST, MIRRTEXT, OSNAPCOORD, ATTDIA.
tools.usage:
SYSVARMONITOR
(System Variable Monitor dialog: table Variable / Preferred / Current / Status; Reset All; Edit List...; Enable balloon notification; status bar icon)
SYSMON = 0 off | 1 on

parameters.name: Preferred value
parameters.description: Set per variable in the list; the current value is compared at each change.

parameters.name: Edit List
parameters.description: Add/remove variables from the monitored set (only user-settable variables).

parameters.name: status-bar icon
parameters.description: Turns into an alert when a variable deviates; click to open the monitor.

tools.example:
SYSVARMONITOR
(Edit List: add OSMODE, preferred 4133; Enable balloon notification; OK)
; when a LISP sets OSMODE 0 and forgets to restore it, a balloon appears and Reset All fixes it
tools.notes: The monitor cannot block changes, only report and reset them. The Express Tool SYSVDLG covers saving/restoring whole sets of variables to a file.

tools.name: SYSVDLG
tools.description: Express Tool that opens the System Variables dialog listing every system variable with its current value, initial value, whether it is saved in the drawing or registry and its description, allowing values to be edited, a set of variables to be saved to a .svf file and restored later, and two states compared. CAD managers use it to snapshot a clean configuration and to reset a user's session; it also lists variables that no longer exist in the documentation.
tools.usage:
SYSVDLG
(System Variables dialog: list with filter; Details: New Value, Current Value, Initial Value, Saved In, Description; Save All..., Save Selected..., Read..., Compare...)

parameters.name: .svf
parameters.description: Plain-text file of variable = value lines; Read applies it, Compare shows differences against the session.

parameters.name: Saved In
parameters.description: Drawing, Registry, or Not saved - tells you whether a value travels with the DWG.

tools.example:
SYSVDLG
(Save All... C:\std\clean_config.svf)
; later on a misconfigured seat
SYSVDLG (Read... clean_config.svf)
tools.notes: Read-only variables are skipped when restoring. The .svf includes drawing-saved variables, so restoring in a drawing changes that drawing. Not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: FILETAB
tools.description: Shows the file tabs strip above the drawing area (2014+), one tab per open drawing with a modified asterisk, a lock icon for read-only files, thumbnail previews of model and layouts on hover (FILETABPREVIEW, FILETABTHUMBHOVER), drag-to-reorder and a plus button for new drawings; FILETABCLOSE hides the strip and FILETABSTATE reports it. Right-click a tab for New, Open, Save, Save As, Save All, Close, Close All, Close All Other, Copy Full File Path, Open File Location.
tools.usage:
FILETAB / FILETABCLOSE
FILETABSTATE = 0 | 1 (read-only)
FILETABPREVIEW = 0 list of layouts | 1 thumbnails on hover
FILETABTHUMBHOVER = 0 | 1 (switch to the hovered layout temporarily)
NEWTABMODE (legacy) / Start tab plus button behaviour

parameters.name: drag out
parameters.description: 2022+: dragging a tab out of the main window creates a floating drawing window (SYSFLOATING).

parameters.name: Ctrl+Tab
parameters.description: Cycles drawings regardless of tab display.

tools.example:
FILETABCLOSE
(more vertical space on a laptop)
FILETAB
tools.notes: Tabs are part of the application, not the drawing; their state is stored in the profile. Very many open drawings collapse tabs into a drop-down at the right end of the strip.

tools.name: GOTOSTART
tools.description: Switches to the Start tab (2016+), the launch page with New (template picker), Open, recent files with thumbnails and pinning, the Autodesk Docs / connected folders list, sheet sets, notifications and (2025-2026) a Learning & Insights page; STARTMODE decides whether the Start tab exists at all. It is what the Home icon on the file-tab bar does, and scripts can use it to leave all drawings without closing them.
tools.usage:
GOTOSTART
STARTMODE = 0 Start tab hidden | 1 Start tab displayed (default)
STARTUP = 0 no Start tab, new drawing opens | 1 legacy Startup/Create New Drawing dialogs | 2 Start tab (default) | 3 Start tab plus a new drawing

parameters.name: Recent
parameters.description: Recent documents list with grid/list view, filters, pin, and 'Remove from list'; the count is set in OPTIONS > Open and Save.

parameters.name: Templates drop-down
parameters.description: Quick pick of templates next to the New button; Get More Templates Online.

tools.example:
STARTMODE 1
GOTOSTART
tools.notes: The Start tab was redesigned in 2022 and again in 2024/2026 (Insights page). In the Core Console and with /nologo it is irrelevant. Autodesk Docs content on the Start tab requires the Desktop Connector or a sign-in.

tools.name: COLORTHEME
tools.description: Sets the interface colour theme - dark (0) or light (1) - for the ribbon, palettes, status bar, file tabs and dialogs (2015+; the dark theme was refreshed in 2024 and 2025). It does not change the drawing area background, which is set per context (2D model space, sheet/layout, Block Editor, command line) in OPTIONS > Display > Colors, nor the crosshair colour.
tools.usage:
COLORTHEME = 0 (Dark) | 1 (Light)
OPTIONS > Display > Color scheme: Dark / Light  (same setting)

parameters.name: 0 Dark
parameters.description: Default since 2015; matches the dark model-space background.

parameters.name: 1 Light
parameters.description: Classic light UI.

tools.example:
COLORTHEME 1
; and a white drawing background via OPTIONS > Display > Colors > 2D model space > Uniform background = White
tools.notes: Stored in the profile (registry). Custom ribbon button images should be provided in both light and dark variants (CUI supports image pairs) to stay readable in either theme.

tools.name: LOCKUI
tools.description: Locks the position and size of toolbars and palettes so they cannot be moved or resized accidentally: a bit sum for docked toolbars (1), docked palettes/windows (2), floating toolbars (4) and floating palettes/windows (8); 0 unlocks everything. The padlock icon in the status bar offers the same choices, and holding Ctrl temporarily unlocks for a drag.
tools.usage:
LOCKUI = bit sum: 0 none | 1 docked toolbars | 2 docked windows | 4 floating toolbars | 8 floating windows  (e.g. 15 = lock all)
Status bar > padlock icon > Floating Toolbars / Docked Toolbars / Floating Windows / Docked Windows / All

parameters.name: Ctrl override
parameters.description: Hold Ctrl while dragging to move a locked element temporarily.

tools.example:
; CAD manager profile: lock docked elements only
LOCKUI 3
tools.notes: Ribbon panels are not covered (they follow the workspace). The setting is saved in the profile and travels with the .arg export.

tools.name: QUICKPROPERTIES
tools.description: Toggles the Quick Properties panel (Ctrl+Shift+P), a small floating palette that appears next to selected objects showing their most-used properties (layer, colour, length, text contents, block name...) for immediate editing without the full Properties palette. Which properties appear per object type is customised in CUI > Quick Properties; QPMODE controls the mode and QPLOCATION where the panel appears; the status-bar button toggles it.
tools.usage:
QUICKPROPERTIES  (toggles on/off)
QPMODE = 0 off | 1 on for all objects | 2 on only for objects with Quick Properties defined in CUI (default) | negative = off but remember the mode
QPLOCATION = 0 float near the cursor (with Idle time and Height settings in DSETTINGS > Quick Properties) | 1 fixed position (last dragged location)
DSETTINGS > Quick Properties tab: Display the Quick Properties palette on selection, Palette Location, Palette Behavior (collapse, minimum rows)

parameters.name: CUI > Quick Properties
parameters.description: Per object type, tick the properties shown; 'Apply to all object types' for general ones.

parameters.name: collapse
parameters.description: The panel shows a few rows and expands on hover when 'Collapse palette automatically' is set.

tools.example:
QPMODE 1
(select a text; change its Contents in the Quick Properties panel; Esc)
tools.notes: Quick Properties and Rollover Tooltips share the CUI definitions. Many users disable it (QPMODE 0) because it pops up during window selections; PROPERTIES remains the full editor.

tools.name: ADCNAVIGATE
tools.description: Opens DesignCenter (Ctrl+2) directly at a given folder, drawing file or network path, so a macro or LISP can present a block library without the user browsing; ADCCLOSE closes DesignCenter and ADCSTATE reports whether it is open. DesignCenter itself (ADCENTER) browses the named objects - blocks, layers, styles, layouts, xrefs - of any drawing on disk and lets them be dragged into the current drawing or onto tool palettes.
tools.usage:
ADCNAVIGATE
Enter pathname <last>: <folder | file.dwg | \\server\share\lib>
ADCCLOSE
ADCSTATE = 0 | 1 (read-only)

parameters.name: pathname
parameters.description: A folder shows its drawings; a .dwg opens its named-object tree (Blocks, Dimstyles, Layers, Layouts, Linetypes, Multileaderstyles, Tablestyles, Textstyles, Visualstyles, Xrefs).

parameters.name: Create Tool Palette
parameters.description: Right-click a folder or drawing in DesignCenter to turn all its blocks into a palette.

tools.example:
; CUI macro: open the symbol library
^C^C_ADCNAVIGATE;\\cadserver\lib\symbols.dwg
tools.notes: DesignCenter reads drawings without opening them, so it works on read-only libraries. The Blocks palette (2020+) Libraries tab covers block insertion more conveniently; DesignCenter remains for layers, styles and layouts.

tools.name: COUNT
tools.description: Counts the instances of a selected block (or of geometry identical to a selected set of objects) in the whole drawing or within a defined area (2022+): the matches are highlighted, a Count toolbar shows the number with previous/next navigation (COUNTNAVPREV/COUNTNAVNEXT), an error indicator for overlapping or exploded instances (COUNTERRORNUM, COUNTCHECK) and buttons to insert the count as a field (COUNTFIELD) or exit (COUNTCLOSE). COUNTAREA (2023) restricts the count to a polygon, and SELECTCOUNT (2023) selects all counted objects.
tools.usage:
COUNT
Select objects: <a block reference or a group of objects to match> Enter   (Enter with nothing selected counts every block, opening the Count palette)
(Count toolbar: < > navigate, count number, error badge, Insert Field, Exit; the Count palette adds Create Table)
COUNTAREA  Specify first corner point / polygon of the count area
COUNTNAVNEXT / COUNTNAVPREV / COUNTFIELD / COUNTCLOSE / SELECTCOUNT

parameters.name: COUNTCHECK
parameters.description: Bit sum of error types to flag: overlapping instances, exploded blocks, renamed/nested copies.

parameters.name: COUNTCOLOR / COUNTERRORCOLOR
parameters.description: Highlight colours of counted objects and of potential errors.

parameters.name: COUNTNUMBER / COUNTERRORNUM
parameters.description: Read-only current count and error count (usable in LISP after a count).

parameters.name: COUNTSERVICE
parameters.description: 1 keeps a background index of blocks so counts are instant; 0 disables it for slow machines.

tools.example:
COUNT
(pick one CHAIR block) Enter
-> 24 instances highlighted, 1 error (exploded copy) - step to it with the arrows
COUNTFIELD (click in the legend to place '24')
COUNTCLOSE
tools.notes: Counting geometry (not blocks) matches exact copies in any rotation/scale. Counts include all model-space instances regardless of layer visibility; xref content is excluded. Available in AutoCAD LT and the web app.

tools.name: COUNTLIST
tools.description: Opens the Count palette (2022+) listing every block definition in the drawing with its instance count, searchable and sortable, with a per-row count-in-drawing action and the Create Table button that runs COUNTTABLE to insert a table of block names and counts (with a live field per count). COUNTLISTCLOSE closes it and COUNTPALETTESTATE reports its state. It is the modern take-off tool replacing BCOUNT and DATAEXTRACTION for simple block schedules.
tools.usage:
COUNTLIST  (Insert tab / Home tab > Count; or Enter at the COUNT prompt)
(Count palette: search box, Name / Count columns, row context menu Count in Drawing, Insert Count Table)
COUNTTABLE  Specify insertion point: <point>  (table with Name and Count columns; counts are COUNT fields)
COUNTLISTCLOSE

parameters.name: Insert Count Table
parameters.description: Choose which blocks to include; the table uses the current table style; counts update with UPDATEFIELD/REGEN.

parameters.name: nested blocks
parameters.description: Only top-level references in model space are counted.

tools.example:
COUNTLIST
(search DOOR; tick DOOR_900 and DOOR_1200; Insert Count Table; click in the legend)
; later, after adding doors:
UPDATEFIELD ALL
tools.notes: Dynamic blocks are counted by definition name (all visibility states together). For attribute-based schedules DATAEXTRACTION remains necessary.

tools.name: TRACE
tools.description: Trace (2022+): a virtual tracing-paper overlay in which collaborators sketch markups (lines, revision clouds, text, imported PDFs/images) without touching the drawing's own geometry; traces are saved in the DWG, created in the AutoCAD web/mobile apps or on the desktop (since 2023) and reviewed through the Trace palette. TRACE at the command prompt creates, opens, closes, deletes or renames traces by keyword; TRACEEDIT / TRACEVIEW (2023) switch the active trace between contributing and viewing, TRACEFRONT / TRACEBACK put the trace or the drawing in front, and COPYFROMTRACE (2024) copies trace objects into the drawing.
tools.usage:
TRACE  (command-line trace management: options to create a New trace, Open an existing one by name, Close the active trace, Delete or Rename traces - the keywords are listed at the prompt)
TRACEEDIT / TRACEVIEW   (edit the trace vs. edit the host drawing while the trace is visible)
TRACEFRONT / TRACEBACK  (which is drawn saturated: the trace or the host)
COPYFROMTRACE  Select objects in the trace: ... (copies into the drawing)
System variables: TRACEMODE (0 none active, 1 editing, 2 viewing), TRACECURRENT (name), TRACEOSNAP, TRACEFADECTL, TRACEPAPERCTL, TRACEDISPLAYMODE

parameters.name: trace contents
parameters.description: Any 2D object can be drawn in a trace; objects have a trace-specific colour scheme; the host drawing is read-only while TRACEMODE is 1.

parameters.name: TRACEOSNAP
parameters.description: 1 lets object snaps acquire trace geometry while viewing (TRACEMODE 2).

parameters.name: TRACEFADECTL / TRACEPAPERCTL
parameters.description: Fading of the inactive layer (host or trace) and opacity of the tracing-paper effect.

tools.example:
TRACEPALETTEOPEN
(click New Trace; name 'Review 03'; draw revision clouds and notes)
TRACEVIEW
(edit the host drawing with the trace still visible)
COPYFROMTRACE (select the note text) -> becomes real MTEXT
tools.notes: Traces are stored with the drawing and visible to anyone opening it in 2022+ (older releases ignore them). Trace geometry never plots. Not available in the Core Console.

tools.name: TRACEPALETTEOPEN
tools.description: Opens the Trace palette listing the traces in the current drawing with author, date and thumbnail; from it you create a new trace, open one for viewing or editing, rename, delete, and (with Markup Import) see imported markups. TRACEPALETTECLOSE closes it and TRACEPALETTESTATE reports the state. The palette is also where the tracing-paper toggle and the trace settings (fade, opacity, snap to trace) live.
tools.usage:
TRACEPALETTEOPEN  (Collaborate tab > Trace)
(palette: New Trace, list of traces with hover actions Open/Edit/Rename/Delete, settings gear)
TRACEPALETTECLOSE

parameters.name: New Trace
parameters.description: Creates and activates a trace in edit mode (TRACEMODE 1).

parameters.name: Open
parameters.description: Activates in view mode; use the ribbon's Edit Trace or TRACEEDIT to contribute.

tools.example:
TRACEPALETTEOPEN
(open 'Client comments 12-03'; TRACEBACK to see the drawing saturated; step through the clouds)
tools.notes: Only one trace can be active at a time. Trace names must be unique within the drawing.

tools.name: MARKUPIMPORT
tools.description: Imports a marked-up copy of the drawing - a PDF, PNG or JPG that someone red-lined on paper, in Autodesk Docs or in another viewer - as a new trace aligned over the drawing (2023+), matching it automatically to the geometry so the markups sit in the right place; the markup 'paper' can be shown or hidden (MARKUPPAPERDISPLAY) and faded (MARKUPPAPERTRANSPARENCY). -MARKUPIMPORT is the command-line form. From 2026 markups made by collaborators in Autodesk Docs/AutoCAD web appear here for review as well.
tools.usage:
MARKUPIMPORT
(Select Markup File dialog: .pdf / .png / .jpg; multi-page PDFs ask for the page)
(the markup is placed and aligned automatically; if alignment fails: Specify alignment points on the drawing and the markup)
-MARKUPIMPORT  Enter file name: <path>  ...
MARKUPPAPERDISPLAY = 0 | 1 ; MARKUPPAPERTRANSPARENCY = 0-100

parameters.name: alignment
parameters.description: Automatic matching of the raster/PDF to the drawing extents; manual two-point alignment fallback.

parameters.name: trace
parameters.description: The import creates a trace named after the file; it appears in the Trace palette.

tools.example:
MARKUPIMPORT
(choose PLAN_review_marked.pdf, page 1)
MARKUPASSIST (click a red-lined note to insert it as MTEXT)
tools.notes: Works best with markups made on a plot of the same layout at the same scale. Image size limits apply (large scans should be downsampled). Not in the Core Console.

tools.name: MARKUPASSIST
tools.description: Analyses an imported markup with machine learning (2023+) and identifies its elements - handwritten or typed text, revision clouds, leaders, strike-throughs, crossed-out objects - outlining each with a box; clicking a box offers to insert the element as native MTEXT, MLEADER or REVCLOUD (text recognised by OCR, editable before placing), to copy it, or to fade/hide it with FADEMARKUP once handled. MARKUPASSISTMODE toggles the highlighting, MARKUPSELECTIONMODE lets the boxes act as selection criteria, and COMMENTHIGHLIGHT shows badges for PDF comments (2024).
tools.usage:
MARKUPASSIST  (Collaborate tab > Markup Assist; on/off toggle)
(hover an identified markup; click: Insert as Text / Insert as Multileader / Insert as Revision Cloud / Copy Text / Fade)
-MARKUPASSIST  (command-line analysis)
FADEMARKUP / -FADEMARKUP  Select markups to fade: ...
MARKUPASSISTMODE = 0 | 1 ; MARKUPSELECTIONMODE = 0 | 1 ; TRACEMARKUPFADECTL = fade amount

parameters.name: Insert as Text
parameters.description: Recognised characters placed as MTEXT at the markup location (edit in the pop-up first).

parameters.name: Insert as Revision Cloud
parameters.description: A REVCLOUD around the same extents on the current layer.

parameters.name: Fade
parameters.description: Dims the handled markup in the trace so remaining work stands out.

tools.example:
MARKUPIMPORT (review.pdf)
MARKUPASSIST
(click the cloud around the stair: Insert as Revision Cloud; click the note 'ADD HANDRAIL': Insert as Multileader, pick the arrow point; Fade both)
tools.notes: Recognition needs an internet connection for the ML service in some releases and is limited to Latin scripts for OCR. Results are suggestions - check dimensions and numbers. The markups remain in the trace as reference.

tools.name: SHARE
tools.description: Shares a copy of the current drawing (2021+) as a link that opens in the AutoCAD web app, either view-only or editable (the recipient saves their own copy), packaging the drawing with its xrefs, images and fonts so the link is self-contained; links expire after seven days. It replaced e-mailing DWGs for quick reviews, and the recipient needs only a browser (an Autodesk account for editing). Requires signing in and an internet connection.
tools.usage:
SHARE  (Collaborate tab > Share; Quick Access toolbar Share icon)
(Share dialog: View only / Edit and save a copy; Copy link; Send link by e-mail)

parameters.name: View only
parameters.description: Recipient can view, measure, print and comment but not save changes.

parameters.name: Edit and save a copy
parameters.description: Recipient can edit in the web app and save the drawing to their own Autodesk account.

parameters.name: package
parameters.description: Xrefs, images, underlays and fonts are included automatically (like ETRANSMIT).

tools.example:
QSAVE
SHARE
(View only; Copy link; paste into the client e-mail)
tools.notes: The shared copy is a snapshot at the time of sharing. For persistent collaboration store the drawing in Autodesk Docs and share from there. Not in the Core Console.

tools.name: SHAREVIEW
tools.description: Shared Views (2019+): publishes a lightweight representation of the current view or of the whole drawing (all model and layout content) to the Autodesk Viewer in the cloud and returns a link that anyone can open in a browser without AutoCAD, with tools to view, measure, mark up and comment; comments come back into the Shared Views palette (SHAREDVIEWS). Views expire after 30 days unless extended. -SHAREVIEW is the command-line form; SHAREVIEWTYPE and SHAREVIEWPROPERTIES set what is included.
tools.usage:
SHAREVIEW
(Share View dialog: Name; Share current view only / Share model view and all layout views; Create 2D views only; Share object properties; Share)
-SHAREVIEW  Enter view name: ... options as above
SHAREDVIEWS  (palette: list of shared views with thumbnails; View in browser, Extend, Delete, comments thread)
SHAREDVIEWSCLOSE
SHAREVIEWTYPE = 0 current view | 1 model and all layouts ; SHAREVIEWPROPERTIES = 0 | 1

parameters.name: Share object properties
parameters.description: Includes property data so the viewer's Properties panel can show layer/object details (larger upload).

parameters.name: Create 2D views only
parameters.description: Skips the 3D representation for faster processing.

parameters.name: Comments
parameters.description: Reviewers' comments and replies are shown in the palette with links to the location in the view.

tools.example:
SHAREVIEW
(Name: Issue 03 review; Share model view and all layout views; Share)
(link appears; copy to the reviewers)
SHAREDVIEWS (read comments; reply; Extend the expiry)
tools.notes: Requires an Autodesk account; the upload is processed in the cloud and can take minutes. The original DWG is never shared, only the view representation.

tools.name: PUSHTODOCSOPEN
tools.description: Opens the Push to Autodesk Docs palette (2022+), which uploads selected layouts of the current drawing as PDF sheets to a folder in an Autodesk Docs (ACC/BIM 360) project, using the layouts' page setups, so the construction team sees current sheets without a manual plot-and-upload cycle. PUSHTODOCSCLOSE closes it; PUSHTODOCSSTATE reports the state; ENABLESYNCPDF (2025) embeds source-drawing information in PDFs saved to Docs so markups can be traced back.
tools.usage:
PUSHTODOCSOPEN  (Collaborate tab > Push to Autodesk Docs)
(palette: sign in; choose Project and Folder; tick layouts; Push)
PUSHTODOCSCLOSE
ENABLESYNCPDF = 0 | 1

parameters.name: layouts
parameters.description: Each selected layout becomes one PDF (or one multi-sheet PDF depending on the settings) named after the layout.

parameters.name: page setup
parameters.description: The layout's own page setup is used; set a PDF pc3 and CTB beforehand.

tools.example:
PUSHTODOCSOPEN
(Project: 1042 Office; Folder: Sheets/For Review; tick A1-01..A1-06; Push)
tools.notes: Requires the Autodesk Docs entitlement and sign-in; large sets push in the background. The drawing itself can live anywhere - only PDFs are uploaded.

tools.name: SAVETOWEBMOBILE
tools.description: Saves a copy of the current drawing (with its xrefs and images packaged) to your Autodesk account storage so it can be opened in the AutoCAD web app and mobile app; OPENFROMWEBMOBILE opens a drawing from that storage (2019+). Together with Autodesk Docs and the Desktop Connector these are the built-in bridges between the desktop and the web/mobile products.
tools.usage:
SAVETOWEBMOBILE
(Save to AutoCAD Web & Mobile dialog: folder in Autodesk Drive/Docs; name; Save)
OPENFROMWEBMOBILE
(Open from AutoCAD Web & Mobile dialog: browse the cloud folders; Open)

parameters.name: packaging
parameters.description: Xrefs, images and fonts are uploaded with the drawing so it displays correctly on the web.

parameters.name: Autodesk Drive
parameters.description: Personal cloud storage that comes with the subscription; Docs projects appear when you have access.

tools.example:
SAVETOWEBMOBILE
(folder: Site visits; Save)
(on the phone: open the drawing in AutoCAD mobile, add a trace)
OPENFROMWEBMOBILE (open it back on the desktop; review the trace)
tools.notes: Edits made on the web are saved to the cloud copy, not to the local file; download or open from web to merge. Requires sign-in.

tools.name: ACTIVITYINSIGHTSOPEN
tools.description: Opens the Activity Insights palette (2024+), a chronological log of events for the current drawing - opened, saved, plotted/published, xrefs attached or changed, renamed or copied in Windows Explorer, and which user and version did it - read from a local event database (ACTIVITYINSIGHTSPATH) that can be shared on a network so a whole team's activity is visible. In 2026 a 'What's changed' action compares the drawing with a previous saved activity using DWG Compare. ACTIVITYINSIGHTSCLOSE closes it; ACTIVITYINSIGHTSSUPPORT (2025) disables the feature; ACTIVITYINSIGHTSVIEWEDLOGGING controls logging of view-only opens.
tools.usage:
ACTIVITYINSIGHTSOPEN  (View tab > History > Activity Insights)
(palette: filter by event type / user / date; event rows with details; 2026: What's changed on save events)
ACTIVITYINSIGHTSCLOSE
ACTIVITYINSIGHTSPATH = folder of the event database (default %LOCALAPPDATA%\Autodesk\ActivityInsights\Common)
ACTIVITYINSIGHTSSUPPORT = 0 off | 1 on
ACTIVITYINSIGHTSVIEWEDLOGGING = 0 | 1

parameters.name: shared database
parameters.description: Point ACTIVITYINSIGHTSPATH of all users to one network folder to consolidate events.

parameters.name: event types
parameters.description: Open, Save, Plot, Publish, Xref changes, File system rename/copy/move, Version (Docs), Viewed.

tools.example:
ACTIVITYINSIGHTSOPEN
(filter: Save events, last 7 days; hover the Friday save; click 'What's changed' -> COMPARE against that version)
tools.notes: Events are recorded only by AutoCAD 2024+ sessions with the feature enabled; there is no history for older activity. Privacy: usernames are logged - disable with ACTIVITYINSIGHTSSUPPORT 0 where required.

tools.name: ASSISTANTOPEN
tools.description: Opens the Autodesk Assistant palette (2024.1+): a search and chat interface over the help, forums and knowledge base that, in 2025-2026, became an AI assistant answering questions about features and workflows and offering support options (chat with an agent, request a callback, create a case) without leaving AutoCAD. ASSISTANTCLOSE closes it, ASSISTANTSTATE reports its state and ASSISTANTSUPPORT (2026) set to 0 disables the assistant entirely for organisations that prohibit it.
tools.usage:
ASSISTANTOPEN  (Help drop-down > Autodesk Assistant; also reachable from F1 help)
ASSISTANTCLOSE
ASSISTANTSTATE = 0 closed | 1 open | 2 hidden (read-only)
ASSISTANTSUPPORT = 0 disabled | 1 enabled (2026)

parameters.name: languages
parameters.description: Available for English, German and Japanese installations at launch.

parameters.name: sign-in
parameters.description: Support actions (chat, cases) require an Autodesk account with support entitlement.

tools.example:
ASSISTANTOPEN
(type: 'how do I make a block annotative' - read the answer; click the linked help topic)
tools.notes: The assistant does not execute commands in the drawing; it answers questions and links to help. It requires an internet connection.

tools.name: COMMANDMACROS
tools.description: Opens the Command Macros palette (2023+), which shows macro recommendations derived from the command sequences you repeat (Macro Insights) and lets you turn them into saved command macros that run with one click, plus your own macros created from scratch; each macro is a command string like a CUI macro and can be edited, renamed and added to the ribbon. COMMANDMACROSCLOSE closes it; MACROINSIGHTSSUPPORT and MACRONOTIFY control whether sequences are analysed and whether the notification appears; COMMANDMACROSSTATE reports the palette state.
tools.usage:
COMMANDMACROS  (Manage tab > Command Macros)
(palette: Insights tab with suggested macros [Try / Save]; My Macros tab [Run, Edit, Rename, Delete, Add to ribbon])
COMMANDMACROSCLOSE
MACROINSIGHTSSUPPORT = 0 | 1 ; MACRONOTIFY = 0 | 1

parameters.name: macro string
parameters.description: Standard macro syntax (^C^C_layiso;;_zoom;_e) recorded from your command history.

parameters.name: privacy
parameters.description: Insights rely on usage analytics; disable MACROINSIGHTSSUPPORT to stop the analysis (the palette still works for manual macros).

tools.example:
COMMANDMACROS
(Insights: 'LAYISO then ZOOM Extents' - Save as 'Isolate & zoom'; Add to ribbon)
tools.notes: Macros are stored per user (not in the drawing) and are simpler than Action Recorder macros - no pauses for input beyond the backslash. Requires sign-in for insights.

tools.name: PERFANALYZER
tools.description: Opens the Performance Analyzer palette (2023.1+) that records how long each command and operation takes in the session, highlights slow ones and generates a report (HTML/text) with system, drawing and add-in information that can be sent to Autodesk support or used by a CAD manager to find the LISP routine or xref that makes a drawing sluggish. PERFANALYZERCLOSE closes it.
tools.usage:
PERFANALYZER
(palette: Start/Stop recording; list of operations with durations; Generate Report; Settings)
PERFANALYZERCLOSE

parameters.name: report
parameters.description: Includes hardware, graphics settings (GRAPHICSCONFIG), loaded applications, drawing statistics and the timing table.

parameters.name: PMTOGGLE
parameters.description: Older Performance Recorder (2015+) that captures a session log for support - superseded by the analyzer.

tools.example:
PERFANALYZER
(Start; open the slow drawing; run REGEN and a few edits; Stop; Generate Report -> C:\support\perf.html)
tools.notes: Recording adds small overhead; stop it when done. The report may contain file paths and user names.

tools.name: HIGHLIGHTNEW
tools.description: Controls whether new and changed features of the release and its updates are highlighted in the interface with an orange dot/badge (ribbon buttons, dialog items) linking to their help topics (2017.1+); SHOWNEWSTATE reports whether highlighting is currently active. Turn it off in deployments so users are not distracted, or use it right after an upgrade to discover what changed.
tools.usage:
HIGHLIGHTNEW
Enter an option [ON/OFF] <ON>:
SHOWNEWSTATE = 0 | 1 (read-only)
tools.example:
HIGHLIGHTNEW
OFF
tools.notes: The highlight database is part of the product update; it does not require a network connection. The What's New page on the Start tab is the fuller list.

tools.name: APPSTORE
tools.description: Opens the Autodesk App Store website (2018+) where free and paid add-ins for AutoCAD are published; apps download as installers that place a .bundle folder (with a PackageContents.xml manifest) in the ApplicationPlugins folder, which the Autoloader loads at startup - the same mechanism organisations use to deploy their own .NET/LISP/ARX add-ins without editing acad.lsp or the registry. Installed apps appear on the Add-ins ribbon tab.
tools.usage:
APPSTORE  (opens https://apps.autodesk.com in the browser)
Autoloader bundle layout:
  %PROGRAMDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins\MyApp.bundle\PackageContents.xml
  ...\Contents\MyApp.dll  /  MyApp.lsp  /  MyApp.cuix
PackageContents.xml: <ApplicationPackage SchemaVersion="1.0" ProductCode="{GUID}" Name="MyApp" AppVersion="1.0"> <Components> <RuntimeRequirements SeriesMin="R24.0" Platform="AutoCAD*"/> <ComponentEntry AppName="MyApp" ModuleName="./Contents/MyApp.dll" LoadOnAutoCADStartup="True"> <Commands GroupName="MYAPP"><Command Local="MYCMD" Global="MYCMD"/></Commands> </ComponentEntry> </Components> </ApplicationPackage>

parameters.name: ApplicationPlugins folders
parameters.description: %PROGRAMDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins (all users) and %APPDATA%\Autodesk\ApplicationPlugins (current user).

parameters.name: APPAUTOLOAD
parameters.description: System variable bit sum: 1 load on startup, 2 when a new drawing opens, 4 when the plug-in appears - 0 disables the Autoloader.

tools.example: ; deploy an in-house LISP as a bundle: create the folder, the XML with a ComponentEntry ModuleName="./Contents/tools.lsp", restart AutoCAD - the commands are available without APPLOAD
tools.notes: Bundles are also what Design Automation for AutoCAD expects as AppBundles. Apps from the store are signed; SECURELOAD applies to their LISP/ARX content (the ApplicationPlugins folders are trusted).

tools.name: ACTUSERINPUT
tools.description: While recording an action macro with ACTRECORD, inserts a request for user input at that point, so that on playback the macro pauses for the user to supply the point, value or selection instead of replaying the recorded one; ACTUSERMESSAGE inserts a message box shown during playback, ACTBASEPOINT inserts a base point, and ACTSTOP saves the .actm file. The Action Recorder panel's tree shows each recorded command with its values, where right-click also converts values to Request User Input or Pause for User Input.
tools.usage:
ACTRECORD
(perform commands)
ACTUSERINPUT   (the next recorded value becomes a user-input request)
ACTUSERMESSAGE  Enter message: <text>
ACTBASEPOINT   Specify base point: <point>
ACTSTOP        (Action Macro dialog: name, description, restore pre-playback view, check for inconsistencies; the .actm is saved in ACTRECPATH)
ACTPLAY  Enter action macro name or [?]: <name>

parameters.name: ACTRECPATH / ACTPATH
parameters.description: Folder where new macros are saved and additional folders searched for playback.

parameters.name: ACTUI
parameters.description: Bit sum controlling the Action Recorder panel expansion during record/playback.

parameters.name: Insert user message / Pause
parameters.description: Editable afterwards in the Action tree (right-click a node).

tools.example:
ACTRECORD
LAYER (make DIM current)
ACTUSERINPUT
DIMLINEAR (pick two points, place)
ACTUSERMESSAGE
Pick the dimension points now
ACTSTOP -> name DIMONLAYER

ACTPLAY DIMONLAYER
tools.notes: Action macros record command input, not LISP or dialogs (dialog interactions are recorded as command-line equivalents where possible). They are simpler than scripts for end users but less portable than LISP; not in AutoCAD LT.

tools.name: SYSFLOATING
tools.description: Reports and controls the dock state of drawing windows in the floating drawing windows feature (2022+): file tabs can be dragged out of the main AutoCAD window to become independent floating windows - on a second monitor, for instance - each with its own command line and drawing area while sharing the ribbon and palettes; SYSFLOATING 0 means the tabs are docked in the main window, 1 that floating windows are in use. Right-click a file tab and choose Move to New Window / Move to Main Window for the same effect.
tools.usage:
SYSFLOATING = 0 (all drawing windows docked in the application window) | 1 (one or more floating drawing windows)
File tab right-click: Move to New Window / Move to Main Window; drag a tab outside the main window

parameters.name: floating window features
parameters.description: Own title bar, command line, status bar; Ctrl+Tab still cycles; the ribbon in the main window acts on the active drawing.

parameters.name: limitations
parameters.description: Palettes stay with the main window; some dialogs open on the main monitor.

tools.example:
(drag the DETAILS.dwg tab to the second monitor)
SYSFLOATING -> 1
tools.notes: Floating windows are a session state, not saved in the drawing; the profile remembers the last arrangement. Not applicable to the Core Console.

tools.name: WEBLOAD
tools.description: Loads a JavaScript file from a URL and executes it (2014+) using the AutoCAD JavaScript API, an HTML/JS route for simple palettes and web-based tools; the URL's domain must be listed in TRUSTEDDOMAINS or the load is refused (SECURELOAD applies). The JavaScript API is limited (no direct database access - it calls commands and LISP) and has seen little development since 2016, so .NET (NETLOAD) or the AutoCAD web app's own APIs are the recommended routes for new work.
tools.usage:
WEBLOAD
Enter URL of JavaScript file: <https://server/app.js>
TRUSTEDDOMAINS = "domain1.com;domain2.com"  (domains allowed to run JavaScript and web content)

parameters.name: TRUSTEDDOMAINS
parameters.description: Semicolon-separated list; the default allows only Autodesk domains.

parameters.name: Acad JavaScript API
parameters.description: Functions such as Acad.Editor.executeCommandAsync and modeless palettes via HTML pages (WEBLOAD hosts them in the embedded browser).

tools.example:
TRUSTEDDOMAINS
tools.example.com
WEBLOAD
https://tools.example.com/legend.js
tools.notes: The embedded browser follows the Windows WebView; scripts that manipulate the drawing still go through commands. Prefer LISP or .NET unless the tool is a thin web front-end.
